_about: Every lemma the Tamarin theories must prove, and what each is for. formal/check.py refuses a run whose lemmas are not exactly these: one missing, one more, one twice, one incomplete or one falsified fails it. A lemma is added or retired here, with its reason, in the same change as the theory.

lemmas.name: can_finish_a_handshake
lemmas.claim: Reachability: two honest Macs finish a handshake with the same keys, hash and master, with no key given away.
lemmas.assumes: none

lemmas.name: can_deliver_a_record
lemmas.claim: Reachability: a record the sender sealed is written by the receiver.
lemmas.assumes: none (for the purpose `drop`, carrying the handshake hash)

lemmas.name: can_resume
lemmas.claim: Reachability: a resume is asked for, accepted and confirmed.
lemmas.assumes: none (carrying the handshake hash)

lemmas.name: an_ephemeral_secret_is_never_known
lemmas.claim: Helper: a Mac's ephemeral secret is never derivable by the attacker.
lemmas.assumes: ideal AEAD, DH, hash and HKDF (symbolic model)

lemmas.name: a_static_secret_is_known_only_by_being_given_away
lemmas.claim: Helper: a static secret is known to the attacker only after an explicit compromise of that key.
lemmas.assumes: ideal AEAD, DH, hash and HKDF (symbolic model)

lemmas.name: a_probe_is_answered_by_the_key_it_reports
lemmas.claim: A probe's answer was made, for this probe's own ephemeral, by a Mac that holds the key it reports.
lemmas.assumes: a peer key that some Mac made (Static) and that was not given away before the handshake finished

lemmas.name: master_is_secret_for_the_initiator
lemmas.claim: Session-key secrecy, forward secrecy and no key-compromise impersonation, as the initiator sees it: master is never known to the attacker.
lemmas.assumes: a peer key that some Mac made (Static) and that was not given away before the handshake finished; this Mac's own key may be known; either key may be given away afterwards

lemmas.name: master_is_secret_for_the_responder
lemmas.claim: The same as the responder sees it.
lemmas.assumes: a peer key that some Mac made (Static) and that was not given away before the handshake finished; this Mac's own key may be known; either key may be given away afterwards

lemmas.name: transport_keys_are_secret_for_the_initiator
lemmas.claim: Both transport keys of the control channel are never known to the attacker, as the initiator sees it.
lemmas.assumes: a peer key that some Mac made (Static) and that was not given away before the handshake finished

lemmas.name: transport_keys_are_secret_for_the_responder
lemmas.claim: The same as the responder sees it.
lemmas.assumes: a peer key that some Mac made (Static) and that was not given away before the handshake finished

lemmas.name: the_responder_agrees_with_the_initiator
lemmas.claim: Mutual authentication with injective agreement: when the responder finishes, exactly one initiator with the key it names finished the same handshake (same keys, hash, transport keys and master); a finished handshake cannot be replayed into a second.
lemmas.assumes: a peer key that some Mac made (Static) and that was not given away before the handshake finished

lemmas.name: the_initiator_agrees_with_the_responder
lemmas.claim: When the initiator finishes, the responder it names answered this very handshake.
lemmas.assumes: a peer key that some Mac made (Static) and that was not given away before the handshake finished

lemmas.name: the_handshake_hash_binds_both_static_keys
lemmas.claim: Two Macs that hold the same handshake hash each hold the other's real static key and the same master. No condition on who knows what. (NimbusPairing.spthy assumes exactly this of the hash the codes are made from.)
lemmas.assumes: none beyond ideal AEAD, DH, hash and HKDF (symbolic model)

lemmas.name: the_responders_master_is_one_handshake
lemmas.claim: Isolation between sessions: any initiator holding the responder's master is the one it finished with.
lemmas.assumes: the initiator's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac

lemmas.name: the_initiators_master_is_one_handshake
lemmas.claim: The same from the initiator's end.
lemmas.assumes: the responder's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac

lemmas.name: only_the_sender_attaches_a_data_connection
lemmas.claim: Proof of possession at attach: a data connection is taken only from the Mac that holds the drop's keys, for that connection number and the challenge this receiver made.
lemmas.assumes: the sender's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac; the drop's own handshake finished at the receiver; a key given away after that is no excuse

lemmas.name: what_is_written_is_what_the_sender_sealed
lemmas.claim: Integrity of what reaches the disk, as far as the cryptography goes: what is written is what the sender sealed, under that header, on that connection, at that count.
lemmas.assumes: the sender's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac; the drop's own handshake finished at the receiver

lemmas.name: a_chunk_is_secret
lemmas.claim: Confidentiality of file contents: a chunk is never known to the attacker.
lemmas.assumes: the receiver's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac; the drop's own handshake finished at the sender

lemmas.name: only_the_sender_resumes_a_drop
lemmas.claim: Authorisation of a reconnect: a drop is picked up again only by the Mac that holds its keys, on the handshake the proof was made for.
lemmas.assumes: the sender's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac; a key given away after the drop began is no excuse

lemmas.name: only_the_receiver_confirms_a_resume
lemmas.claim: The sender takes `resumed` only from the receiver of that drop.
lemmas.assumes: the receiver's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac; a key given away after the drop began is no excuse

lemmas.name: can_probe_and_hang_up
lemmas.claim: Reachability: a probe proves the responder's key and no initiator finishes.
lemmas.assumes: no key given away

lemmas.name: can_say_what_a_connection_is_for
lemmas.claim: Reachability: both hellos cross and agree on the purpose.
lemmas.assumes: no key given away

lemmas.name: can_run_a_speed_test
lemmas.claim: Reachability: one record each way on two connections of one speed test.
lemmas.assumes: no key given away

lemmas.name: can_finish_when_the_initiators_own_key_was_given_away
lemmas.claim: Reachability of the key-compromise-impersonation case: two Macs finish a handshake though the initiator's own key leaked first.
lemmas.assumes: the responder's key never given away

lemmas.name: the_handshake_hash_binds_the_openings
lemmas.claim: Two ends with the same handshake hash saw the same openings: nobody chose the protocol major for them.
lemmas.assumes: none beyond ideal AEAD, DH, hash and HKDF (symbolic model)

lemmas.name: a_handshake_hash_is_one_initiators
lemmas.claim: Replay: no two initiator handshakes finish with the same handshake hash.
lemmas.assumes: none beyond ideal AEAD, DH, hash and HKDF (symbolic model)

lemmas.name: a_handshake_hash_is_one_responders
lemmas.claim: The same for responders.
lemmas.assumes: none beyond ideal AEAD, DH, hash and HKDF (symbolic model)

lemmas.name: the_responders_master_is_no_other_responders
lemmas.claim: Isolation between sessions: no other responder handshake holds this master.
lemmas.assumes: the initiator's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac

lemmas.name: the_initiators_master_is_no_other_initiators
lemmas.claim: Isolation between sessions: no other initiator handshake holds this master.
lemmas.assumes: the responder's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac

lemmas.name: both_ends_agree_what_a_connection_is_for
lemmas.claim: Separation by purpose: the purpose the responder acts on (drop, pair, verify, resume, retire, speed) is the one the initiator said on this handshake.
lemmas.assumes: the initiator's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac

lemmas.name: the_initiator_hears_only_the_responder
lemmas.claim: Separation by direction: the hello the initiator reads was said by the responder after finishing this same handshake.
lemmas.assumes: the responder's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac

lemmas.name: a_chunk_is_written_only_under_its_own_header
lemmas.claim: A chunk is written only under the header the sender sealed it with.
lemmas.assumes: the sender's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac

lemmas.name: what_a_speed_test_counts_is_what_the_other_mac_sealed
lemmas.claim: What the tester counts was sealed by the Mac it asked, for this test, on that connection.
lemmas.assumes: the responder's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac

lemmas.name: what_is_sealed_for_one_purpose_is_never_written_for_another
lemmas.claim: Isolation between a speed test and a file transfer: anything sealed with the bytes that were written was sealed for the same purpose, handshake and master.
lemmas.assumes: the sender's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac; one handshake has one purpose (the sealed hello)

lemmas.name: what_a_speed_test_sends_back_is_never_written
lemmas.claim: No record a speed test's responder sealed is written to disk by any receiver.
lemmas.assumes: the sender's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac

lemmas.name: a_sealed_chunk_is_written_only_where_it_was_sealed_for
lemmas.claim: Isolation between transfers: a sealed chunk is written only by that Mac, on that handshake, connection, count and header.
lemmas.assumes: the receiver's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac; one record per connection in the model

lemmas.name: a_sealed_chunk_is_written_once
lemmas.claim: Replay: a sealed chunk is written at most once anywhere (stated from the sender's view).
lemmas.assumes: the receiver's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac; a connection number is claimed once (the model's Once restriction: ReceiveSession.claim)

lemmas.name: what_is_written_is_secret
lemmas.claim: What the receiver wrote is not known to the attacker.
lemmas.assumes: the sender's key was made by a Mac and not given away before the handshake the lemma is about finished at this Mac

lemmas.name: two_people_can_pair
lemmas.claim: Reachability: two people who read and type the codes pair their two Macs.
lemmas.assumes: none

lemmas.name: a_stored_pairing_is_with_the_mac_the_person_meant
lemmas.claim: Pairing binds identity: whatever a Mac stores as the Mac its person was pairing with is that Mac's own key, in either role, in any number of pairings at once, with someone in the middle of every connection who hears the codes and can steer a short code whenever they hold its last input.
lemmas.assumes: the people read the codes truthfully over a channel the attacker hears but cannot alter; the handshake hash binds both static keys (proved in NimbusHandshake.spthy); a short code agrees by luck with probability outside a symbolic model (formal/computational/pairing-bound.md)

lemmas.name: two_people_can_pair_by_number
lemmas.claim: Reachability: two people who enter each other's identity numbers both store.
lemmas.assumes: none

lemmas.name: the_mac_that_asked_stores_one_exchange
lemmas.claim: The Mac that asked stores only for an exchange the other Mac showed its code for: the same handshake hash, Ns and Nr.
lemmas.assumes: the people type only what the Mac they mean shows; the attacker steers a short code only while it holds the code's last input

lemmas.name: the_mac_that_was_asked_stores_one_exchange
lemmas.claim: The same from the Mac that was asked.
lemmas.assumes: the people type only what the Mac they mean shows; the attacker steers a short code only while it holds the code's last input

_not_settled: Four mutant flags in NimbusHandshake.spthy are NOT in formal/check.py because the search did not finish within 12 GB, for or against: NoConnInStreamKey (and with it NoHeaderBinding), NoHashInResume, SameResumeLabel. Nothing is claimed of what the lemmas say about those four guards; the Swift tests and scripts/mutate.py are what holds them.
